requirement:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234

#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

story.summary: Makes the type-collection code more tolerant of bad key layouts. Before, two members with the same key, or a mix of int and string keys, could throw inside the analyzer. Now it reports the diagnostic and skips the offending member. It adds analyzer tests for `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]` types, two execution tests, and a README section on opting out of source generation.
story.why: Issue 2234 says the analyzer stops working for types with `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` since 3.1.1. The agent's fix assumes the cause is an exception in `TypeCollector`. The likely candidates are `Dictionary.Add` on a duplicate key and `intKey!.Value` on a null key after the mixed-key diagnostic. Either would abort analysis and hide all other diagnostics.
touches_beyond_requirement: README.md gains a new 'Opting out of source generation' section that commits to which analyzer rules do and do not apply to suppressed types.
The `TypeCollector` change applies to all `[MessagePackObject]` types, not only suppressed ones. A test covers a normal generated type too.
The execution tests check runtime round-tripping through the dynamic resolver and that no generated formatter exists. That is generator/runtime behavior, not the analyzer.
story.confidence_overview: The crash-avoidance edits are high confidence: they are small and local. Confidence that they fix the reported regression is low to medium. Nothing in the diff touches a `SuppressSourceGeneration` code path, and the issue does not say which diagnostics went missing. The suppressed-type tests for MsgPack004, MsgPack015 and MsgPack003 may pass with or without the source change; the diff does not show that.

claims.text: After reporting the mixed int/string key diagnostic, the collector now skips that member with `continue`. It no longer falls through to `intKey!.Value` or the string path with a null key, which could throw.

claims.text: The README documents which analyzer rules apply to suppressed types. It lists MsgPack012 as still enforced, but no test in the diff covers MsgPack012 for suppressed types.

The analyzer tests check that suppressed types still get MsgPack004 (missing key), MsgPack015 (`AllowPrivate` required), MsgPack003 (member type not serializable) and MsgPack005 (duplicate or mixed keys). These are the behaviors the requirement says broke. The diff does not show that any of these tests fail without the source change.

refusals.what: The source fix is generic crash avoidance for duplicate and mixed keys. It has no change tied to `SuppressSourceGeneration`.
refusals.why: It is unclear whether this addresses the reported regression or a different crash. A human should confirm the root cause against the 3.1.0 to 3.1.1 diff or a repro from the issue.

refusals.what: The README adds documentation that commits to which analyzer rules run for suppressed types.
refusals.why: It is a documentation commitment beyond the bug fix, and part of it (MsgPack012) is unverified by tests.

findings.description: No change in the diff is specific to `SuppressSourceGeneration`. The fix only guards against duplicate/mixed-key crashes, which also affect non-suppressed types, as the `ForGeneratedTypes` test shows. If the 3.1.1 regression was really caused by suppressed types skipping analysis or taking a different code path, this change does not address it. Nobody has confirmed the root cause.

The `continue` skips the rest of the loop body for that member. That includes the formatter-attribute lookup at line 1045 and any later per-member checks. Other diagnostics for a member with a mismatched key kind may no longer be reported.

Duplicate-key members are now silently dropped from the member map. This is safe only if MsgPack005 is an error that blocks the build. If a user lowers its severity, the generator would emit a formatter that quietly omits the duplicate member.

The MsgPack004, MsgPack015 and MsgPack003 suppressed-type tests exercise no changed code, because the source change only affects duplicate and mixed keys. They may pass without the fix, so they do not show that the reported regression is resolved.

Runtime round-trip and no-generated-formatter tests. These cover generator and runtime behavior, not the analyzer named in the requirement.
